This database schema is named rschema_0360 and it consists of three tables: Log, Operator, and Operation_Log.
The Log table represents a log of system activities. It has five columns: Log_Category (a string of up to 255 characters), Log_Content (a string of up to 255 characters), Log_Creation_Time (a date and time), Log_Deletion_Time (a date and time), Log_ID (an integer, primary key), and Log_Last_Modified_Time (a date and time).
The Operator table is used to store information about the users who can access the system. It has four columns: Account (a string of up to 255 characters), Contact_Information (a string of up to 255 characters), ID (an integer, primary key), and Password (a string of up to 255 characters).
The Operation_Log table is a log of operations performed by users. It has five columns: Execution_Content (a string of up to 255 characters), Log_ID (an integer, foreign key referencing the Log table), Operation_Time (a date and time), Operation_Type (a string of up to 255 characters), and User_ID (an integer, foreign key referencing the Operator table). The primary key of this table is a composite of Log_ID, User_ID, and Operation_Time.
This schema ensures referential integrity, as all foreign keys reference primary keys in their respective tables. It also ensures entity integrity, as each table has a primary key. The schema is exhaustive, covering all the necessary tables and their columns, and their relationships.
gold_question: The business requirements description for the log management system: The system is designed to record and manage operational logs, supporting the creation, modification, and deletion of logs. The system must capture detailed information for each log, including log level, content, category, and lifecycle (creation, modification, and deletion timestamps). Each log operation must be associated with an operator, who possesses an ID, account, password, contact information, permissions, and user role. By recording the relationship between logs and operators, the system can track the operational history of each log, including operation time, operation type, and execution content. Additionally, the system supports categorized management of logs to ensure the traceability and integrity of log data.
ddl:
-- Schema for database: rschema_0360
CREATE TABLE `log` (
  `log_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `log_category` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `log_content` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `log_creation_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `log_deletion_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `log_last_modified_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`log_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `operator` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `account` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `contact_information` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `password` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `operation_log` (
  `log_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `operation_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `execution_content` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `operation_type` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`log_id`, `user_id`, `operation_time`),
  CONSTRAINT `operation_log_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`log_id`) REFERENCES `log` (`log_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `operation_log_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `operator` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
